canonical_statement: The universe's evolution in the phantom phase does not necessarily end in a singularity, as non-singular cosmological models exist.

attributions.surface_quote: singularity is not the only possible ending of the evolution of the universe in the phantom phase

canonical_statement: An increase in the Hubble parameter near a singularity leads to an increase in the universe's temperature.

attributions.surface_quote: increase of the Hubble parameter near the singularity leads to an increase of the universe temperature

canonical_statement: Thermal radiation in the late Universe is caused by Hawking radiation generated on the visible horizon.

attributions.surface_quote: Thermal radiation is here caused by the Hawking radiation generated on the visible horizon

canonical_statement: The viscosity of the cosmic fluid affects the behavior of the universe near a singularity and must be considered for accurate descriptions.

attributions.surface_quote: viscosity of the cosmic fluid also affects the behavior of the universe near the singularity

canonical_statement: Entropic cosmology posits a connection between gravity and thermodynamics.

attributions.surface_quote: approach to a modified theory of gravity is specifically based on the connection between gravity and thermodynamics

canonical_statement: In entropic cosmology, the entropy function generates the energy density and pressure in the Friedmann equations.

attributions.surface_quote: entropy function generates the energy density and pressure in the Friedmann equations

canonical_statement: The Friedmann equations can be derived from the fundamental laws of thermodynamics.

attributions.surface_quote: Friedmann equations are derived from the fundamental laws of thermodynamics

canonical_statement: In the late stage of the universe's evolution, if the cosmological constant is zero, dark energy density is entirely generated from entropy energy density.

attributions.surface_quote: dark energy density is entirely generated from the entropy energy density

canonical_statement: The standard cold dark matter model is effective at cosmological scales but problematic at galactic scales due to the assumption of no pressure.

attributions.surface_quote: standard cold dark matter model provides very efficient results at very large (cosmological) scales, but its application might be problematic at galactic scales

canonical_statement: The accelerated expansion of the universe requires the pressure of the fluid to be negative.

attributions.surface_quote: accelerated expansion of the universe, it is necessary that the pressure of the fluid specified in terms of the EoS is negative

canonical_statement: The universe can experience future finite-time singularities.

attributions.surface_quote: future finite time singularities can appear.

canonical_statement: Big Rip singularities are the most destructive type of cosmological singularity.

attributions.surface_quote: A cosmological singularity of the (BR) type is most destructive.

canonical_statement: All types of singularities are fundamentally classical in nature.

attributions.surface_quote: All types of singularities are purely classical singularities in nature.

canonical_statement: An increase in the Hubble function leads to an increase in temperature.

attributions.surface_quote: an increase of the Hubble function leads to an increase of the temperature.

canonical_statement: Thermal radiation near a singularity is associated with Hawking's radiation.

attributions.surface_quote: The nature of this thermal radiation is associated with Hawking’s radiation

canonical_statement: Hawking's radiation is generated on the apparent horizon of the FLRW universe.

attributions.surface_quote: generated on the apparent horizon of the FLRW universe.

canonical_statement: Hawking's radiation is linked to the existence of visible horizons in black holes and cosmic events.

attributions.surface_quote: associated with the existence of the visible horizon of the black hole, as well as the visible horizon of cosmic events

canonical_statement: Hawking's thermal spectrum radiation appears in the late universe at high temperatures before its Rip time.

attributions.surface_quote: Hawking’s thermal spectrum radiation shows up in the late universe, at high temperatures, shortly before its Rip time.

canonical_statement: Accounting for thermal radiation can qualitatively change the classical description of singularities and create a more realistic picture of the future universe.

attributions.surface_quote: Accounting for thermal radiation will allow a qualitative change in the classical description of the singularity and creates a more realistic picture of the future universe.

canonical_statement: Thermal radiation energy density is proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.

attributions.surface_quote: the thermal radiation energy density is proportional to the fourth power of the absolute temperature.

canonical_statement: Near a future singularity, where the Hubble parameter increases without limit, dark energy density can be represented as proportional to the fourth power of the Hubble parameter.

attributions.surface_quote: near the future singularity, where the Hubble parameter increases without limit, one can phenomenological represent the dark energy density as ρ rad = λ H 4

canonical_statement: The Hayward-Kodama temperature describes the temperature of the horizon in cosmology, incorporating both the Hubble parameter and its derivative.

attributions.surface_quote: the temperature of the horizon in cosmology is given by Hayward-Kodama temperature which contains both the Hubble parameter and its derivative.

canonical_statement: If the universe continues to expand with acceleration, it will approach de Sitter space-time, where a cosmological horizon will radiate like a black hole's event horizon.

attributions.surface_quote: If the universe continues to expand with acceleration... the universe will approach de Sitter space time, where there will be a cosmological horizon that radiates in the same way as the event horizon of a black hole generates Hawking radiation.

canonical_statement: A cosmological singularity of the Big Rip type occurs when the Hubble function tends to infinity at a finite time.

attributions.surface_quote: If t tends to a finite value... then H → ∞, and a cosmological singularity of the Big Rip type appears.

canonical_statement: The Hubble function tends to a cosmological constant as time approaches infinity.

attributions.surface_quote: In the limit t → ∞ the Hubble function tends to the cosmological constant.

canonical_statement: The universe can experience multiple singularities, which are points of infinite density or curvature.

attributions.surface_quote: The time tmax corresponds to the occurrence of a new singularity.

canonical_statement: The timing of cosmic singularities is not fixed and can vary based on physical models and parameters.

attributions.surface_quote: The time of possible occurrence of singularities has again changed.

canonical_statement: Cosmological models can exhibit finite scale factors, energy densities, and effective pressures, avoiding certain types of singularities.

attributions.surface_quote: the values of the scale factor, energy density and effective pressure turn out to be finite

canonical_statement: The absence of diverging higher derivatives of the Hubble function indicates the avoidance of cosmological finite-time singularities.

attributions.surface_quote: higher derivatives of the Hubble function do not diverge. ... no cosmological finite-time singularity is here formed.

canonical_statement: A type III singularity occurs when a specific parameter tends to zero, resulting in finite scale factor but diverging effective energy and pressure.

attributions.surface_quote: if the parameter b tends to zero, then the scale factor is finite, but the effective energy and pressure diverge. This case corresponds to a type III singularity

canonical_statement: Type III singularities are milder than Type I but stronger than Type II singularities.

attributions.surface_quote: a type III singularity, which is milder than a Type I, and stronger than a Type II.

canonical_statement: Thermal radiation can influence a transition between different types of cosmological singularities.

attributions.surface_quote: A transition from singularity types, from Type I to Type III, is here possible, due to the influence of thermal radiation.
